We use relative clauses or relative pronouns to include extra information about someone or something in the sentences.
About...
Words
Examples
People
Who
Jake, who is the GOAT athlete, is here.
Places
Where
The club, where Sarah went legless, is closing.
Things
Which
The house, which the busybody bought, is great.
Time
When
Tonight, when I see my jellybean, I’ll confess my love.
Reasons
Why
I don’t know why he is so wishy - washy about this.
Belonging
Whose
Joe, whose party was so dismal, has another one this weekend.
To Consider
1. Most relative pronouns are enclosed between commas. 

2. They can also be used as the example with why. 

3. How can be used to set clauses related to manners or ways.  E.G: I know how he did it!
4. We can also used that to create relative clauses for people and things.

Jane, that lives here, is my best friend.
The car, that is on the corner, was stolen yesterday.

The house, which the busybody bought, is great.
Tonight, when I see my jellybean, I’ll confess my love.
I don’t know why he is so wishy - washy about this.
Joe, whose party was so dismal, has another one this weekend.

Jane, that lives here, is my best friend.
The car, that is on the corner, was stolen yesterday.

I know someone who would love to see you!

 I want to know how you did this (working as complement)
She did amazing , how she normally does, that night at the concert.(emphatic information)
All clauses can work like this

Everybody remembers him and I really don’t know why they are always comparing me to him; I guess, it may be all about what he did and how he was. Honestly, I haven’t had not even half of his experience here, it is not what I expected; I should be looking for another job where my best friend suggested, but I cannot remember exactly what he said that is why I am calling him tomorrow.
